intent: Correct user-rejected Ly, Le and Nguyen architecture and match restrained capital footprints

jobs.brief:
Subject: Lý royal precinct, Thăng Long, 11th–12th century, a source-informed interpretation of lost buildings. Image 1 is the REJECTED edit target; image 2 is the scale/style reference.
REPLACE the giant curled ends with small restrained ceramic ridge ornaments and modest eave lifts. DELETE every tall freestanding ornament/chimney post and DELETE the rear central building. Main hall: broad low single-storey timber hall with a shallow ochre-yellow tiled roof, vermilion columns and low cream plinth. Two smaller green-tiled side halls flank it. A modest red-tiled timber gate sits in the foreground. Small ground-level covered galleries can connect the sides, each with clear timber posts below a continuous simple roof; never a staircase-shaped green ramp. Low warm brick wall and plain capped corners, no tall finials. Exactly four main buildings: hall, two side halls, gate. A clear modest central courtyard, a physically consistent same-level plan. One roof per building, with the main hall only about 1.5 times a side hall's width. Use documented Lý green/yellow glazed tile colors and small dragon/phoenix/lotus motifs, not speculative ornate spirals or later Huế structures. Royal elegance comes from a balanced restrained composition.
jobs.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: one Vietnamese historical capital sprite for a small RTS map.
The user rejects the target as unreal architecture and too big. REDRAW the architecture substantially; retaining the rejected silhouette is not success. Preserve the Vietnamese Đông Hồ woodblock adaptation: warm dark ink, flat ochre/terracotta/red and muted green pigments, crisp compact silhouettes. Use the supporting Đinh sprite ONLY as a reference for restrained eaves, building scale and drawing language.
Make a coherent, plausible royal precinct at miniature map scale. All halls rest on low foundations on one ground level, with visible doors, short usable stairs and clear ground-level circulation. No aerial walkways, giant ramps, floating roofs, stacked palace terraces, chimney-like posts, ornamental spirals, or invented tiers. The main hall is larger through width, never a giant multi-storey mass; its eave height should be close to the side buildings. Roof corners have modest lifted tips and very small period-appropriate ornaments. Fewer architectural units with clean structural joins.
Camera front-centered orthographic elevated 30 degrees, no yaw, matching the game. Complete compact contour, target visible width/height 1.18–1.25. Fit inside a square canvas with a generous 8% empty margin. Palette vivid but restrained; no photographic lighting, excessive hatching or 3D render.
Output ONE sprite with TRUE transparent alpha outside and through empty courtyards. No painted checkerboard, paper rectangle, paved ground slab, water, scenery, text, labels, people, flags, or comparison panels. Opacity belongs only to real architecture. Do not simply shrink the old drawing within the canvas: redraw its proportions and structure.

jobs.brief:
Subject: Lê royal precinct, Đông Kinh, 15th-century reference, illustrative reconstruction of the lost hall. Image 1 is the REJECTED edit target; image 2 is the restrained scale/style reference.
REMOVE the entire rear tier of three buildings and ALL tall retaining terraces. Use only one royal timber hall at the rear, two low narrow side galleries at ground level, and the foreground Đoan Môn-inspired masonry gateway. Keep a usable open courtyard between hall and gate. The main hall is ONE occupied storey with a restrained low double-eaved yellow-tile roof, not two storeys stacked on a platform. Its shallow plinth carries exactly THREE parallel stair approaches separated and bounded by FOUR small stone dragon balustrades; these are low stairs, not a mountain of steps. A broad low brick-and-stone front gateway has EXACTLY FIVE arched passages, two left of centre and two right of centre, with a plain low parapet and NO roof pavilion sitting on it. It must not become a Roman aqueduct: the openings sit naturally at ground level without long projecting individual stair ramps. Side enclosures are simple low walls. No Hanoi Flag Tower, no later pagoda, no other towers, no rear palace rising above the main roof. Preserve beautiful ochre-gold roofs and vermilion timber while reducing every ornamental tip to a small architectural detail. Main hall width about 65% of full gateway width. Keep the whole silhouette compact and in the same size class as the Đinh reference.

jobs.brief:
Subject: Nguyễn imperial precinct, Huế after 1833. Image 1 is the REJECTED edit target. Image 2 is a restrained drawing/scale reference. Image 3 is an official photograph of the REAL Ngọ Môn used for architectural geometry only, not night colors or light.
Replace the impossible compound of tall platforms and overhead stone connections with TWO grounded architectural landmarks: the real Ngọ Môn gateway in front, and a low Thái Hòa audience hall behind, separated by a clear ground-level courtyard. DELETE the rear red palace, DELETE both rear corner pavilions, DELETE ALL elevated side bridges and long stone ramps. Only short low enclosure wall returns at the sides, with no invented roofs.
Ngọ Môn must follow the photograph's broad low U-shaped platform: three central front passages (gold door at centre, red side doors), solid front ends of the projecting wings, with the two remaining historical entrances on the SIDE returns, not front-facing. Do NOT draw five forward-facing arches. Above it is the continuous Ngũ Phụng timber pavilion: a low continuous lower roof with a shallow central upper roof and low wing roof groups, not two giant isolated towers. Its documented upper roof groups are nine total, central yellow and eight green; at this miniature size simplify details while retaining the coherent connected roof arrangement. No giant roof curls or huge dragons.
Thái Hòa behind is ONE low occupied timber storey with linked front/rear roof volumes (trùng thiềm điệp ốc), ochre-yellow tiles and vermilion columns on a low base. Its eaves remain lower than the top of the gate pavilion; it is not a three-storey palace. Make its roof width about two-thirds of Ngọ Môn's full width. Keep its height modest, the courtyard level and the whole icon compact. This is a compressed representative pair, not a literal complete-city plan. No flags, water or modern structures.
